entry.title: Dansàneu 2026
entry.summary: Proyecto por Toormix Design Agency con 37 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Toormix Design Agency


DANSÀNEU 2026
Dansàneu festival 2026 Campaign

The visual identity for Dansàneu 2026 begins with a gaze. More specifically, with the gaze of the seraphim depicted in the Romanesque paintings of the church of Santa Maria d’Àneu. The eyes on their wings become the starting point for a visual identity that connects heritage, imagination and territory.

Under the concept “The Valls d’Àneu are watching you”, these eyes are reinterpreted and transformed into a graphic element with multiple forms and textures. Iconified, enlarged, combined and transformed, they appear throughout the campaign as a presence that watches over and moves across the Valls d’Àneu, creating a recognisable visual language that can adapt to different communication formats.

The idea takes on a more narrative dimension in the audiovisual spot, where the seraphim’s eyes leave the Romanesque paintings behind and transform into magical characters that come to life. As if they had stepped out of the walls of the church, these figures wander and dance through the Pyrenean landscapes, appearing in some of the locations where the festival performances take place. A way of connecting heritage with the present and making the territory an active part of the story.

The campaign also incorporates a second layer of meaning in the form of a badge. A badge that acts both as a warning and as a statement of reivindication: the right to culture that is accessible to everyone living in the Valls d’Àneu. The project thus highlights the need for a culture that is alive, present and shared throughout the territory, beyond the usual centres of cultural activity.

The badge brings this reivindication from the communication pieces into the physical space and to the people themselves, becoming a tangible element of the campaign. A small symbol worn on the lapel that reivindicates the right to equal access to culture, wherever you live.

The result is a campaign that combines heritage and contemporaneity, imagination and reivindication, expanding Dansàneu’s visual universe while maintaining its strong connection to the territory. A project that comes at a moment of consolidation for the festival, which has increased its audience by almost 30% compared with the previous year, further establishing itself as a high-quality cultural event and a reference in the region for its program and ability to attract audiences.

entry.summary: Brand identity and web design for Modern Funder, an advisory helping founders and operators move from running a company to running a philanthropy.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Numinous Agency®, Geovanie Radcliffe, Artem Shcherban

Brand identity and web design for Modern Funder, an advisory helping founders and operators move from running a company to running a philanthropy.




Modern Funder: 
Brand Identity for a New Kind of Philanthropist


Modern Funder helps operators become deliberate philanthropists.

“As a brand, Modern Funder describes how my clients will feel and act through their work with me.”

That’s what Patrick, founder of Modern Funder, told us, and it became the brief behind everything we built. Not a brand that announces itself. A brand you feel in the work: clear, rigorous, and without the bureaucracy.

Modern Funder grew out of four years of running programs for large foundations at Laurel, still the company behind it. Patrick took the practices established funders rely on and made them work for philanthropists in the making: founders and operators moving from running a company to running a philanthropy.

He didn’t want corporate. He didn’t want institutional. He wanted the rigor of his frameworks to show up in the brand itself, so we built the identity around his process: six phases, Discovery through Operate, each with its own color and icon. The logo, the grid, the guidelines, and the site all play by the same rules.

entry.summary:
In Basque, Zerikusi means “relationship, bond or connection”, but literally translates as “what to see”. Two meanings that reflect its approach to communication: connecting ideas and people through messages that are meaningful and bring value.
To shape the concept, we draw inspiration from the expression “seeing is believing”, highlighting the importance of observing, questioning and understanding before communicating. Because only by asking the right questions can we look beyond the obvious and communicate what truly matters.
The exclamation mark represents that moment when something captures our attention and invites us to see things from a different perspective.
Zerikusi® is an invitation to question in order to connect and communicate with purpose.

entry.title: Pete Buttigieg: A Mosaic of Messages
entry.summary: Six typographic mosaic portraits of Pete Buttigieg by Charis Tsevis (2026), each built from thousands of cut-paper messages: slogans, state names, letters and small images. A positive tribute, free to share under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Charis Tsevis

Six typographic mosaic portraits of Pete Buttigieg by Charis Tsevis (2026), each built from thousands of cut-paper messages: slogans, state names, letters and small images. A positive tribute, free to share under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

Pete Buttigieg: A Mosaic of Messages
Six typographic mosaic portraits by Charis Tsevis, 2026

Pete Buttigieg: A Mosaic of Messages is a series of six mosaic portraits of Pete Buttigieg, made by the Greek artist and designer Charis Tsevis at Tsevis Studio in October 2026. Each portrait is built from 4,068 to 5,556 cut-paper pieces: words and slogans, the names of the fifty states, single letters and small images from American political print. From a distance you see a face. Up close you read a crowd of messages: Hope. Freedom. Common Decency. Neighbors, Not Enemies. Let's Win the Era.

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Quiet Confidence</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55607423610/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

Why Pete
I have supported Pete Buttigieg since 2019. In 2020 I made a series of portraits for his presidential campaign, and I still see in him what I saw then: a calm listener, a debate opener and one of the finest political minds of our time. As mayor of South Bend and as U.S. Secretary of Transportation he showed that politics can be competent, patient and kind at the same time.
I am not partisan. I am not a member of any party, but I always vote, and I openly support a party or a candidate when I choose one: not as a fan, but as a choice for a specific challenge. I believe every society needs all of its parties, because each one represents a real part of it: classes, interests, professions, beliefs and every other social group. Politics is the art of synthesis, and for me the best state is a dynamic equilibrium.
To me, politics is the highest art and science of a society. It has to orchestrate every other discipline: the arts, the sciences, technology, the economy. When politics does not work, societies do not work, and today this is plain to see. Many of our political systems still rest on assumptions and norms that belong to the past, or that simply no longer work.

This is where Pete and I meet. Since his first presidential campaign he has put structural reform first, from reshaping the Supreme Court to amending the Constitution to end the Electoral College. Not as an end in itself, but as the ground for new social contracts: new ways to find common ground, to reach the compromises a democracy needs, and to build synthesis within a nation and between nations.
I have also decided how I support the people I believe in: only in a positive way. I wrote about it in My Art for Politics. These portraits attack no one. Every piece in them says what we could be for, not who we should be against. Some pieces carry the year 2028. Read it as a hope, not as news.

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Eyes on the Horizon</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55607022846/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

A portrait made of messages
A person is never one message. We are made of countless tiles: our history, our work, the hopes of the people around us. In these portraits every tile is a message of its own. 3,406 pieces carry words and slogans, 1,515 are single letters, 761 spell the names of states and 273 are small images: raised fists, flags, barns, columns, faces. Together they form a library of 5,955 messages, and each portrait draws between 2,560 and 3,020 different ones from it.

<div class="caption">256 of the 5,955 pieces in the library.</div>

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Looking Up</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55607423615/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

How it was made
The library. Every piece was designed in the studio from a study of American political posters, signs and print, with the look of letterpress, screen print, hand-painted signs and campaign buttons. I worked with Adobe Creative Cloud and a ComfyUI model that simulates paper, ink and other materials, so that each piece looks cut from a real poster.
The layout. Mozaix, the mosaic software I build, places the pieces with its Jigsaw Packing method: irregular cut shapes fitted edge to edge like a puzzle, larger where the face is calm and smaller, down to 71 pixels, where it needs detail. Each piece is chosen for its color and tone and for the place it takes.

Five layers. Each portrait has five layers: a background, three main layers that form the face, and a detail layer of thin strips that follow the lines, shadows and lights of the face. In the three main layers no piece is used twice.
Each portrait is at least 8,192 × 12,826 pixels, enough for a print of about 69 × 109 cm at 300 dpi.

The full story, with each layer step by step, how the depth of the paper is simulated, the fifty states and many more of the pieces, is on tsevis.com: Pete Buttigieg: A Mosaic of Messages.

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Steady Resolve</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55605996772/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Common Ground</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55607022851/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

<div class="caption"><span class="italic">Pete Buttigieg: Red, Blue and Every Color Between</span>, 2026. High-resolution image can be downloaded from <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/tsevis/55607423315/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</div>

<div class="caption">Detail at full size: every word is a piece of paper.</div>

Free to share
These portraits are free to share for non-commercial use with credit, under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The full-resolution files are on my Flickr. Please don't use them for hate or anything negative. For any other use, see tsevis.com/image-licensing.

Wishing you the best, Pete.

entry.title: MBSL - Intervalle
entry.summary: Proyecto por Tommy Hachez con 15 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Tommy Hachez, Guillaume Beaulieu, Zorani Sanabria, Mambo Mambo




Intervalle, parcours d'art public

Intervalle est un parcours d'art public qui relie une quarantaine d'œuvres dans les rues de Rivière-du-Loup. Le Musée du Bas-Saint-Laurent l'a imaginé comme une invitation à marcher ou à rouler d'une œuvre à l'autre, à ralentir et à regarder la ville autrement.
Le nom parle de ce qui se passe entre deux points. ​​​​​​​On en fait l'inspiration pour l'image de marque. Le mot lui-même devient un chemin, une ligne qui se plie et se déploie, composée de barres qui évoquent les étapes et la multitude des œuvres. Chaque barre agit comme un module. Le système s'allonge, se replie ou se fragmente selon le circuit, le support ou le lieu, et il pourra continuer de grandir avec le parcours.

Intervalle is a public art route linking around forty artworks across the streets of Rivière-du-Loup. The Musée du Bas-Saint-Laurent imagined it as an invitation to walk or ride from one work to the next, to slow down and see the city differently.  The name speaks to what happens between two points. We made it the inspiration for the brand image. The word itself becomes a path, a line that bends and unfolds, made of bars that evoke the stages and the multitude of artworks. Each bar acts as a module. The system stretches, folds or fragments depending on the route, the medium or the location, and it can keep growing along with the route.

entry.title: Puk & Partners
entry.summary: Rebranding for Puk & Partners, an architecture firm that translates brand standards into physical spaces, taking each project from the first design decision to final delivery. A lock-inspired emblem, logotype and visual system built around the firm’s turnkey approach.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Artı Stüdyo, Aksel Ceylan, Kevser Akça, Bora Civelek, Hıdır Yüksel, Eda Kanmaz, Kaan Duygu

Rebranding for Puk & Partners, an architecture firm that translates brand standards into physical spaces, taking each project from the first design decision to final delivery. A lock-inspired emblem, logotype and visual system built around the firm’s turnkey approach.



Puk & Partners

Puk & Partners is an architecture firm that translates brand standards into physical spaces. With an operation network spanning 43 cities across Türkiye, a portfolio of more than 300 projects and partnerships with more than 50 brands. It delivers showrooms and stores for national and global names such as Mercedes-Benz, Lululemon, and Samsung, taking each project from the first design decision to final delivery. For the rebranding, we connected the firm’s name with its way of working and placed this approach at the center of the identity.

Drawing from the meaning of “Puk,” which refers to a lock, we designed an emblem that reinterprets a lock opening through the letter 'P'. A closed form unfolds, much like an idea becoming a space. The lock, key and opening metaphor also expresses Puk’s turnkey approach: a project is carried from first idea to design, application and final detail, then delivered as a completed space. The logotype shares the emblem’s contrasting, anatomical structure, while the custom-designed ampersand (&) reinforces the Partners side of the brand.

The visual language, in turn, draws on architecture itself. A color palette referencing the natural tones of architectural materials plays a key role in the identity. The identity extends across an icon set, technical-drawing-style illustrations, 3D renders with construction-material textures and motion content, as well as workwear for site teams, including vests, helmets and jackets, along with stationery and photography direction.

The result reflects how Puk & Partners practices architecture: taking responsibility from the first decision to the final detail, treating every element as part of a cohesive whole, and carrying each project through to completion.

entry.title: GEOMETRY OF ICE (Part 3)
entry.summary: Abstract ice formations found in ordinary places across Germany, where changing light, sediments and organic material transform frozen surfaces into intricate geometric patterns and shifting fields of color.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Jan Erik Waider

Abstract ice formations found in ordinary places across Germany, where changing light, sediments and organic material transform frozen surfaces into intricate geometric patterns and shifting fields of color.

GEOMETRY OF ICE – Part 3 (→ see Part 1 / Part 2)

What fascinates me about these frozen patterns is how often they appear in surprisingly ordinary places in Germany: shallow puddles, small ponds, frozen streams and wet depressions, many of them found close to Hamburg. The contrast between an unremarkable setting and the complexity that emerges on closer inspection is central to this series. These are not dramatic landscapes, but small surfaces that can easily be overlooked.

The structures only really reveal themselves from the right angle and in the right light. Reflections, sediments, sand, leaves and stones beneath the ice shift the palette from yellow-green and amber through cooler greens and blues to almost monochrome tones. The series is as much about careful observation and changing light as it is about the geometry of ice itself.

entry.title: Emiglia
entry.summary: Proyecto por Another Collective con 37 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Another Collective




Some recipes are passed down through generations. Some names are too.
Emiglia was born from the place where memory meets craft, giving new expression to a story shaped by fresh pasta, time and the pleasure of sharing food.

This rebrand creates a unified identity across both the factory and the pasta bar, allowing the brand to evolve while preserving its human character. The existing illustrations remain an integral part of the system, while a new typographic approach introduces a stronger sense of personality, sitting naturally alongside them and bringing together tradition and contemporary expression with greater confidence.

The logotype reflects this evolution through a warmer, more distinctive design, carrying forward a story that continues to grow with the brand and adapt to new contexts.

From packaging to signage, from menus to everyday communication, every element contributes to a cohesive, approachable and recognisable identity. Craftsmanship is no longer treated as nostalgia, but as a deliberate way of making things. An identity that preserves what matters while finding a new way to express it.
